summary.name: Natron
summary.one_liner: Natron is an open-source, node-based 2D compositing and VFX application with tracking, rotoscoping, keying, and OpenFX plugin support.
use_cases: creating and sharing custom node presets
summary.what_it_does: Natron is a node-based compositing application that uses a workflow similar to Nuke and Fusion, where effects are built by grouping, merging, and connecting nodes. It includes a 2D tracking toolset, a multi-layered rotoscoping tool with per-vertex feathering, and chroma keying with matte refinement. It provides curve and dope-sheet editors for keyframe control. It supports OpenFX plugins, drag-and-drop installation of community PyPlugs (Gizmos), and headless rendering for render farms.
notable: Node-based workflow comparable to Nuke and Fusion
Supports OpenFX (OFX) plug-ins and community PyPlugs/Gizmos
Headless rendering for distributed network rendering
Listed as open-source and freeware in jaywcjlove/awesome-mac
caveats: Latest stable release runs on Apple Silicon only through Rosetta 2; native Apple Silicon support is in an alpha build
Page does not describe Windows or Linux builds; only macOS and FreeBSD are named
